title: Scan load time: 82 ring nodes take 12 s and repair_mesh 1.3 s when opening the segmented crawfish
description:
User report 2026-10-06: loading the segmented crawfish scan takes about 10 s or more, which makes working on it annoying; the user suspected repair_mesh. Measured on fixtures/crawfish_rings.dsl (IMG_4109, 469k vertices / 938k triangles, 82 rings) with run-scene ring-tool: load_mesh 0.26 s, repair_mesh 1.34 s, and the 82 spline_ring nodes 12.0 s together (about 146 ms each, roughly constant per ring, so it grows with every ring the user adds). The graph chains each ring on the previous one's geometry (ring_N = spline_ring(geometry=ring_{N-1}.geometry, ...)). Profile first (run-scene --profile; python3 -m ixdar_automation_cli.async_profile) and name where the per-ring cost goes before changing anything: likely candidates to check, not conclusions, are a copy of the 938k-face bundle per node, rebuilding the surface's geodesic/intrinsic-triangulation structures per node instead of once per surface, per-node edge-mark arrays sized to the whole mesh, and the ring re-trace at full depth. Then make the per-ring cost proportional to the ring, not the mesh, with surface-wide structures built once and shared down the chain. Also look at repair_mesh's 1.3 s (MeshRepair: weld, orient, non-manifold split, degenerates, shells, hole fill) for obvious wins, but the rings are the main target. Results must be identical: same mesh after repair, same ring fingerprints, same region split.

PROFILE (CRAW-57 agent, 2026-10-06, async-profiler cpu + alloc over the full crawfish_rings.dsl load, baseline 3 runs: total 13.1-13.4 s, load_mesh 0.21-0.23 s, repair_mesh 1.21-1.25 s, 82 rings 11.6-12.0 s). Where the per-ring ~146 ms goes: spline_ring rebuilds the whole-surface geodesic engine on every node. SurfaceGeodesics.over is 91% of SplineRingNode.evaluate CPU (1253 of 1382 samples): IntrinsicTriangulation.over 1193 (layOutSignposts/cornerAngle 917, mostly FdLibm acos over all 2.8M half-edge corners; buildConnectivity 247), IntrinsicPathTracer.snapshotOf 30, meanEdgeLengthOf 29. The actual trace (AuthoredSplineRing.trace: geodesics, De Casteljau subdivision) is only 115 samples, about 1.4 ms per ring of real work plus snap. On top of that a third of all CPU samples are inside libjvm (GC): each ring allocates ~260 MB (heap climbs 260 MiB per node in the timing line); the alloc profile puts 68% of all allocation in SurfaceGeodesics.over (IntrinsicTriangulation 62%, the tracer snapshot 6%), 10.6% in the trace's mesh-sized visit buffers and 10% in SurfaceSpline.of -> ConformingLoopSnap (mesh-sized visit stamps, marked-degree and dead-end arrays per ring). No copy of the 938k-face bundle happens: the mesh is passed through by reference. Secondary: SurfaceWaypoints.snap -> NearestVertex.find is a linear scan of all 469k vertices per anchor (65 samples). repair_mesh 1.2 s: MeshRepair.build 138 samples (assemble 47, buildFromIndexedMesh 37, classifyShells 31, ensureEdges/buildEdges 22, orient 18, splitNonManifold 18).

RESULT (CRAW-57 agent). Graph timing, 3 runs each, crawfish_rings.dsl copy, before -> after (ms): load_mesh 234/232/206 -> 217/507/338 (code unchanged; the after runs shared the machine with other agents' scenes); repair_mesh 1225/1249/1210 -> 1274/1489/1481 (code unchanged, same noise); ring_00 (builds the shared structures) 338/353/379 -> 325/320/325; the other 81 rings 11242/11413/11599 -> 780/948/882 (about 141 ms -> 11 ms each); all 82 rings 11580/11766/11978 -> 1105/1268/1207; rings + repair 12805/13015/13188 -> 2379/2757/2688; graph total 13088/13297/13446 -> 2645/3309/3075. Identical results in every after run: repaired-mesh sha256 (mesh-fingerprint), all 82 ring edge-mark fingerprints (ui-state mesh.edgeMarks), and the region split (300 regions, same faces and bounding rings per region). Fertility (fertility_rings.dsl, 13 rings), 8 interleaved A/B runs against master's classes in the same worktree: mesh, 13 ring fingerprints and 10 regions identical; graph median 410 -> 342 ms; rings 2-13 from 8-30 ms median to 2-16 ms; first ring ring_05 median 124 -> 138 ms, within the noise of those runs (load_mesh, unchanged code, went 114 -> 150 ms median in the same pairs). repair_mesh: no obvious win; its 1.2 s is spread over the half-edge build of the output (~0.37 s, per-vertex/per-face IntIdList lists), the shell-containment BVH (~0.23 s; every shell is tested because the report lists containment for dropped shells too), edge building, orient and the non-manifold split. Left for later: after the graph, RingTool.adoptGraphRings re-traces all 82 rings (about 1.1 s plus its own SurfaceGeodesics build) when the ring-tool scene opens; and ConformingLoopSnap still allocates and scans mesh-sized arrays per ring (~5 ms each), which CRAW-49 is restructuring.

Rework (user review, 2026-10-07): no mesh-derived cache. The meshDerived Map<String,Object> on GeometryBundle (string keys, instanceof, casts, re-wrapping in SplineRingNode) is rejected, and so is a lazy value on the mesh: the intrinsic triangulation is too specific a concept to hang on every mesh. Instead: (1) a new mesh node surface_metric(geometry) that computes the surface's intrinsic metric and connection (the signpost intrinsic triangulation: edge lengths, per-vertex signpost angles rescaled to the vertex angle sum, reference half-edges, connectivity, the source-mesh mapping and the unflipped tracer snapshot, plus mean edge length) once and outputs it on a typed port, following cross_field's CROSS_FIELD output; (2) spline_ring gains an optional metric input: given, it uses it; absent, it builds its own as today, so the user's saved fixtures load unchanged; RingDslWriter writes metric= on new saves and the ring scene's graph wires it; (3) RingTool takes the graph's metric instead of building its own engine when the scene opens; (4) a port value is shared by every consumer, so it must be immutable: the base triangulation is never flipped in place; each geodesic works on a private overlay of only the edges it flips (or another approach that keeps the shared base read-only), measured against the current flip-and-undo; SurfaceGeodesics' per-query scratch and last-result arrays become a cheap per-user engine over the shared metric; (5) GeometryBundle returns to master's form (no meshDerived, no withMeshDerived). Keep NearestVertex's grid but build it where it is used (or from the same node if that is cleaner; justify).

REWORK RESULT (CRAW-57 agent, 2026-10-07). Design: SurfaceMetric (paths package) is the surface's intrinsic metric and connection, built once by the new surface_metric node and output on the new SURFACE_METRIC port: the unflipped signpost triangulation (edge lengths, signpost angles, vertex angle sums, reference half-edges, boundary flags, connectivity, source vertex/edge/face mapping), mean edge length, vertex id bound and the NearestVertex grid (kept here because a grid only pays when shared: built per ring it costs more than the scan it replaces, and the ring tool snaps 82 rings' anchors through it). Nothing writes it after SurfaceMetric.of. IntrinsicTriangulation is now a flippable view over a metric: each flip writes a private open-addressed overlay (half-edge next/tail/signpost, edge length, vertex reference half-edge) and reads fall through to the metric; discardFlips clears only the touched slots. The tracer snapshot is gone (IntrinsicPathTracer unfolds the metric's own arrays). SurfaceGeodesics.over(metric) is a per-user engine holding only its overlay, flipper and search buffers; FlipGeodesics' edge occupancy is a path-sized table instead of three mesh-sized arrays, and the A* heap grows on demand. spline_ring takes an optional metric input (absent: it measures the surface itself; a metric of another mesh is refused). surface_metric also outputs geometry, the bundle on the half-edge mesh it measured. RingDslWriter.wireSurfaceMetric (called on every ring-tool save) inserts `surface = surface_metric(geometry=<first ring's input>)` before the first spline ring, rewires that ring to surface.geometry, and adds `metric=surface.metric` to every spline_ring whose geometry chain runs back to it through rings. RingTool takes the graph's metric measured on its surface, else measures one. GeometryBundle is master's again.

Timings, crawfish, interleaved A/B on the same machine state (ms; "before" = the previous rework's shared flip-and-undo engine on the unwired fixture copy, "after" = this design on a wired copy): repair 1196/1433/1365 -> 1296/1292/1439 (unchanged code, noise); engine/metric build (ring_00 incl. engine before, surface_metric after) 325/364/397 -> 210/215/226 (+ ring_00 68/64/82); the other 81 rings 725/701/825 -> 857/804/1022; rings + metric + repair 2246/2498/2587 -> 2431/2375/2769 (all under 3 s). Ring-scene open (RingTool.adoptGraphRings incl. engine, the "gave 82 graph ring(s) anchors" row, now timed from before the engine is readied): 1157/1213/1187 -> 910/756/649. Unwired fixture copy with the new code: rings 9.96 s (each ring measures its own surface, as on master), identical results.

Overlay vs flip-and-undo: the per-ring trace costs about 1.3-2.4 ms more (about 9 -> 10.5 ms). CPU profile of the wired load: overlay find/touch/flipIfPossible about 25 of 1446 samples; the remainder of the difference is each ring's own 7.5 MB of A* visit buffers (the old engine shared them). A private copy of the mutable triangulation per user would allocate about 75 MB per ring, so the overlay is the design kept.

Equality: repaired-mesh sha256, all 82 crawfish ring fingerprints and the region split (300 regions, faces and bounding rings) identical to master in every run, wired and unwired; fertility 13 ring fingerprints, mesh and 10 regions identical in all 15 runs. Fertility per-node medians over 5 interleaved runs, master / new on the unchanged fixture / new wired: total 435/410/309, load 137/125/136, ring_05 134/111/31, ring_06 34/25/12, rings 07-17 within 2-17 ms each; on the unchanged fixture ring_11 and ring_12 medians were 22 and 17 against 14 and 10 (per-run spread 8-34 vs 7-26, GC-dominated); wired every node is faster than master.
definition-of-done:
1. Profile of the current load on the ticket, naming where the per-ring 146 ms goes. 2. The 82-ring crawfish graph evaluates in under 3 s total (rings plus repair), with a per-step before/after table on the ticket. 3. Identical results: repaired mesh fingerprint, all 82 crawfish and 13 fertility ring fingerprints, and the region split (count and per-region faces) unchanged. 4. Small models (fertility) not slower in any node. 5. mvn test passes.

surface_metric node with a typed port; spline_ring's metric input optional; GeometryBundle unchanged from master; the shared metric is never mutated (a test runs two consumers' geodesics interleaved on one metric and gets the same results as separate metrics); timings rerun: rings + repair still under 3 s on the 82-ring crawfish; ring tool open time measured before/after; all fingerprints, the repaired mesh and the region split identical.

Follow-up 2026-10-07 (user's choice): spline_ring's metric input is required. A spline_ring with no metric= fails with an error naming the fix (wire surface = surface_metric(geometry=...)). The fallback where a ring measures the surface itself is deleted. The two tracked files that use spline_ring (dsl/fixtures/crawfish_rings.dsl, dsl/fixtures/fertility_rings.dsl) are rewritten once by the existing wiring (RingDslWriter.wireSurfaceMetric) - wiring statements only, nothing else changes - and load with identical fingerprints and region splits. Every Java test and DSL text that builds a spline_ring is wired.
testing-plan: 1. Baseline and after: run-scene ring-tool on a tmp copy of fixtures/crawfish_rings.dsl, graph timing line per node, 3 runs each. 2. Fingerprint and region-split comparison before/after. 3. Fertility timings before/after.
changes-made: Spline rings share surface-wide structures down the graph: GeometryBundle carries meshDerived structures (kept while the mesh object is the same, dropped by withMesh to another mesh); spline_ring builds the SurfaceGeodesics engine (intrinsic triangulation, tracer, visit buffers) and a new NearestVertex grid once per surface and reuses them, the selection output is set from the ring's marked edges instead of a scan of every edge, and IntrinsicTriangulation computes each corner angle once when laying out signposts. Per-ring cost on the 938k-face crawfish 141 ms -> 11 ms; 82-ring graph rings + repair 13.0 s -> 2.6 s; results identical. New SplineRingChainTest.

Rework: surface-wide structures move off GeometryBundle (back to master's form) into a new surface_metric node whose SURFACE_METRIC port carries an immutable SurfaceMetric (unflipped signpost triangulation, source mapping, mean edge length, vertex grid); spline_ring takes it as an optional metric input, RingTool reuses the graph's metric, the ring tool's save wires one surface_metric into every ring chain, and geodesics flip a private per-engine overlay instead of flipping and undoing a shared triangulation. Crawfish rings + metric + repair 2.4-2.8 s, ring-scene open 1.16-1.21 s -> 0.65-0.91 s, results identical; new SurfaceMetricTest, SplineRingChainTest reworked.

Follow-up: spline_ring's metric input is required; a ring without metric= fails naming the fix (wire surface = surface_metric(geometry=...) and pass metric=surface.metric), and the fallback where a ring measured the surface itself is gone. RingDslWriter.wireSurfaceMetric now wires every spline ring, inserting a surface_metric before any ring whose geometry chain does not run back to one through rings (e.g. after ring_candidates), so a ring-tool save never writes an unloadable graph. fixtures/crawfish_rings.dsl and fertility_rings.dsl rewritten once by that transform (wiring statements only). Tests wired (QuadRingToolTest, RingDeletionTest, SurfaceSplineTest, SplineRingChainTest, which now checks the missing-metric error). Wired loads identical to master: crawfish mesh sha, all ring fingerprints, 300 regions; fertility 13 fingerprints, 10 regions. Timings: crawfish total 2573 ms (surface_metric 169, rings 895, repair 1251); fertility total 332 ms (surface_metric 92, rings 90).
